paragraphs.title: The Dream and the Search for Its Interpretation

answers: At rest in his house and flourishing in his palace
easy.explanation: He says he was at rest in his house and flourishing in his palace.
easy.q: How does Nebuchadnezzar describe his condition at the beginning of the story?

easy.explanation: He says that the dream made him afraid.
easy.q: What caused Nebuchadnezzar to be afraid?

answers: All the wise men of Babylon
easy.explanation: He made a decree to bring all the wise men before him.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar command to explain the dream?

answers: Because he was a military commander
Because the wise men could not interpret the dream
medium.explanation: The wise men were unable to make known the interpretation, so Daniel came before the king.
medium.q: Why was Daniel brought before the king?

answers: The meaning or explanation of the dream
medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar wanted to know the meaning of his dream.
medium.q: What does the word “interpretation” mean in this passage?

answers: Daniel interpreted the dream, and then the king dreamed
The king dreamed, the wise men failed, and Daniel was brought in
The king punished Daniel, and then told him the dream
medium.explanation: The king dreamed, the wise men could not interpret it, and Daniel was summoned.
medium.q: What was the main sequence of events?

answers: He wanted an answer from the learned men of his kingdom
He did not know that Babylon had wise men
He already knew the meaning of the dream
challenge.explanation: He first sought an interpretation from the wise men of Babylon.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king first called the wise men?

answers: Peace at first, followed by fear because of the dream
Wealth at first, followed by famine
War at first, followed by peace
challenge.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar was at rest, but the dream troubled and frightened him.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the beginning and the continuation of the story?

answers: He is presented as having the spirit of the holy gods
He is presented as one of the king's soldiers
He is presented as the builder of the tree
challenge.explanation: The king says that the spirit of the holy gods is in Daniel.
challenge.q: Why is Daniel's spiritual description important when he is introduced?

paragraphs.title: The Mighty Tree and the Angel

easy.explanation: He saw a tree in the midst of the earth.
easy.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar see in his dream?

easy.explanation: Its height reached unto heaven, and its sight reached to the end of the earth.
easy.q: How high did the tree grow?

answers: That it be moved to another land
easy.explanation: The watcher commanded that the tree be cut down.
easy.q: What did the watcher command to be done to the tree?

answers: It served as a place of battle
medium.explanation: The beasts had shade under it, the birds lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed by it.
medium.q: What purpose did the tree serve for living creatures?

answers: The beasts should gather beneath it
The beasts should be removed from beneath it
The beasts should sleep beneath it
medium.explanation: The command says that the beasts should get away from the tree.
medium.q: What does the command “let the beasts get away from under it” mean?

medium.explanation: The stump of its roots was to be left in the earth.
medium.q: What remained after the tree was cut down?

answers: A foundation remained and was not completely destroyed
challenge.explanation: The roots remained in the earth even though the tree was cut down.
challenge.q: What is suggested by leaving the tree's roots in the earth?

answers: His heart would be changed from a man's to a beast's
challenge.explanation: The dream says that a beast's heart would be given to him.
challenge.q: What change was decreed for the one represented by the tree?

answers: Its greatness allowed it to provide for many creatures
Its size kept all creatures away
Its size concerned only its beauty
challenge.explanation: The great tree gave food and shelter to creatures throughout the earth.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the tree's size and its influence?

paragraphs.title: The Interpretation: The King and the Decree

easy.explanation: Daniel told the king, “It is thou, O king.”
easy.q: Whom did the tree represent according to Daniel?

answers: He would be lifted up higher
He would be humbled and driven from men
He would move to another palace
easy.explanation: He would be driven from men and live with the beasts of the field.
easy.q: What would happen to the king because of the decree?

answers: Break off his sins by righteousness and show mercy to the poor
easy.explanation: Daniel urged him to turn from sin and show mercy to the poor.
easy.q: What did Daniel advise the king to do?

answers: Because his kingdom and authority had become very great
Because he lived in a forest
medium.explanation: The tree represented his greatness, dominion, and wide influence.
medium.q: Why was Nebuchadnezzar compared to a great tree?

answers: An extension or delay of peace
medium.explanation: Daniel suggested that repentance might lengthen the king's peaceful condition.
medium.q: What does “a lengthening of thy tranquility” mean?

answers: That the king enlarge his army
That the king know that the heavens rule
That the king plant another tree
medium.explanation: The kingdom would be sure after he recognized that the heavens rule.
medium.q: What condition was emphasized for the kingdom to continue?

answers: The decree humbled a ruler who possessed great authority and pride
challenge.explanation: The dream and its interpretation show the king being brought down from his pride.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between pride and the decree?

answers: He urged the king to make a practical change in his conduct
He taught the king how to build palaces
He explained the structure of the tree
challenge.explanation: Daniel called for both acknowledgment and righteous, merciful actions.
challenge.q: Why did Daniel mention righteousness and mercy along with recognizing supreme rule?

answers: The wise men determine the king's fate
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the decree being called the decree of the Most High?

paragraphs.title: The Fulfillment of the Decree and the King's Boast

easy.explanation: At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of Babylon.
easy.q: How many months passed before Nebuchadnezzar walked in the palace?

answers: Babylon that he had built and his own power
easy.explanation: He boasted about great Babylon, his power, and his majesty.
easy.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar boast about?

easy.explanation: The judgment immediately came upon Nebuchadnezzar.
easy.q: What happened immediately after the voice from heaven?

answers: The king boasted of himself and his work
The wise men interpreted another dream
medium.explanation: The judgment came while the king was boasting about Babylon and his power.
medium.q: What brought about the fulfillment of the decree at that moment?

answers: The place where he would live
medium.explanation: The king's dwelling would be with the beasts of the field.
medium.q: What does “thy dwelling” mean in the passage?

answers: He went from ruling in a palace to living with wild beasts
He changed from a wise man into a commander
He went from being rich to being a poor citizen
medium.explanation: He was driven from men and ate grass like oxen.
medium.q: What change took place in the king's life?

answers: The great humiliation of the king
challenge.explanation: The change shows his fall from a high royal position.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the palace to the field emphasize?

answers: The voice rejected his claim to absolute self-rule
The voice concerned only the city's buildings
challenge.explanation: The voice announced that the kingdom would depart from him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the king's boast and the voice from heaven?

answers: His hair and nails changed, and he was driven from men
challenge.explanation: His appearance changed, and he was separated from human society.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the punishment involved both physical and social change?

paragraphs.title: Restored Understanding and Recognition of Supreme Rule

easy.explanation: He lifted up his eyes unto heaven.
easy.q: Where did Nebuchadnezzar lift his eyes?

easy.explanation: He says that his understanding returned unto him.
easy.q: What returned to him after he lifted his eyes?

easy.explanation: He acknowledged that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men.
easy.q: Who rules in the kingdom of men according to Nebuchadnezzar?

answers: His recognition of heaven came before his understanding returned
He looked to heaven to find Babylon
There is no connection between them
medium.explanation: After he lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned.
medium.q: What is the connection between lifting his eyes to heaven and regaining understanding?

medium.explanation: The word describes the everlasting rule of the Most High.
medium.q: What does “dominion” mean in this passage?

answers: Human rule is limited and depends upon the Most High
The city of Babylon is eternal
medium.explanation: He recognized that God gives kingdoms to whomsoever he will.
medium.q: What acknowledgment did Nebuchadnezzar make?

answers: A change from pride and self-rule to recognition of supreme rule
A change from fear to hatred
A change from poverty to wealth
challenge.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar moved from boasting to acknowledging the authority of the Most High.
challenge.q: What was the central inner change described in these verses?

answers: The rule continues through all generations
The rule belongs to only one generation
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes an enduring dominion.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “from generation to generation” communicate?

answers: All are counted as nothing before the will of the Most High
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that God does according to his will in heaven and on earth.
challenge.q: How does the statement about the inhabitants of the earth support the main idea?

paragraphs.title: The Restoration of the Kingdom and Greatness

easy.explanation: His honor, brightness, and kingdom returned to him.
easy.q: What returned to Nebuchadnezzar after his understanding returned?

easy.explanation: His counsellors and lords sought unto him.
easy.q: Who sought Nebuchadnezzar after his restoration?

easy.explanation: The verse says that excellent majesty was added to him.
easy.q: What was added to the king after his kingdom was restored?

answers: After his understanding returned, his honor and kingdom also returned
The kingdom returned before he lost his understanding
There is no connection between them
medium.explanation: The verse joins the return of his understanding with the restoration of his royal position.
medium.q: What is the connection between restored understanding and restored kingdom?

medium.explanation: It refers to the king's royal splendor and dignity.
medium.q: What does “brightness” mean in this context?

answers: Understanding returned, honor and kingdom returned, and greater majesty was added
The kingdom was lost, the city was built, and understanding returned
The dream came, the tree was cut, and the roots returned
medium.explanation: This is the order stated in the verse.
medium.q: What sequence is described in the verse?

answers: His restoration was more than a return to his former condition
challenge.explanation: The verse says that excellent majesty was added to him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that greater majesty was added to the king?

answers: His counsellors and lords sought him again
The beasts returned to the palace
The wise men left the country
challenge.explanation: The return of the officials showed that his royal position had been restored.
challenge.q: How is the social effect of the king's restoration shown?

answers: Both experience a fall followed by the possibility of continued life or restoration
challenge.explanation: The tree's stump remained, and the king was restored to his kingdom.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the cut tree and the restored king?

paragraphs.title: Praise to the King of Heaven

easy.explanation: He praised, extolled, and honored the King of heaven.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar praise at the end?

easy.explanation: He declared that all his works are truth.
easy.q: How did Nebuchadnezzar describe the works of the King of heaven?

answers: He can hide them from the earth
easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar said that God is able to abase the proud.
easy.q: What can the King of heaven do to those who walk in pride?

answers: It summarizes that the judgment upon the king was just
It describes how Babylon was built
It explains the structure of the tree
medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar recognized that the judgment he received was righteous.
medium.q: How does “his ways judgment” relate to the story of this chapter?

medium.explanation: The verse speaks of those who walk in arrogance.
medium.q: What does “pride” mean in this verse?

answers: He admitted that humbling his pride was justified
He claimed that the punishment never happened
He asked to return to the dream
medium.explanation: After his humiliation, he acknowledged the justice of God's ways.
medium.q: How does the ending relate to the punishment Nebuchadnezzar received?

challenge.explanation: The king concludes that the King of heaven can humble the proud.
challenge.q: What central lesson does Nebuchadnezzar present at the end?

answers: He testified from personal experience of supreme rule
He merely repeated the words of Babylon's wise men
challenge.explanation: He had personally experienced humiliation and restoration, so his words summarize his experience.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the king himself spoke these words of praise?

answers: The kingdom was restored, but recognition of heaven's superiority was the greater lesson
The kingdom returned, so humility was no longer needed
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with restoration joined to recognition of divine justice and authority.
challenge.q: How do the final words complete the theme of the restored kingdom?
